where: Exam traps, third trap ("A four-terminal network is not automatically a two-port; a shared ground that carries current breaks the port condition")
problem: This contradicts Section 1, where the transistor is correctly described as a two-port with the emitter shared between both ports. A three-terminal network whose common terminal returns both port currents does satisfy the port condition: at port 1, I1 enters the base and I1 leaves the emitter; at port 2, I2 enters the collector and I2 leaves the emitter. A student reading both statements cannot tell which one is true.
fix: Say: "A four-terminal network is not automatically a two-port. If the shared terminal also carries current from a third, external path, the port condition fails. A three-terminal device such as a transistor is a valid two-port, because its common terminal carries only I1 and I2."

where: Section 1, third paragraph ("A two-port is linear when its equations contain no powers or products of the port variables. It has no independent sources inside. Any initial stored energy... is zero")
problem: Three separate requirements are stacked in three sentences, and "It" reads as if the linearity definition itself demands no internal sources. Linearity and the source-free / zero-energy conditions are different conditions; only together do they give fixed constants.
fix: Split them: "A two-port is linear when its equations contain no powers, products or constant terms in the port variables. To describe it by four fixed constants, two more conditions are needed: no independent sources inside, and zero initial stored energy in any capacitors or inductors."

where: Section 3, paragraph listing parameter sets ("Choosing V2 and I2 gives the ABCD parameters")
problem: The chapter defines I2 as entering port 2, but standard ABCD (transmission) parameters are written with the current leaving port 2, so the equations and the sign of B and D differ from the textbook form. A student who learned the convention above will get a sign error in ABCD work.
fix: Add one line: "ABCD parameters are normally written with I2 taken as leaving port 2; with the entering convention used here, I2 is replaced by −I2 in those equations."
